items.stem: An inspector finds a part out of tolerance. The correct first action is to:

options.text: Document the nonconformance and segregate the part for disposition
options.rationale: Correct: nonconforming material is recorded and quarantined for a disposition decision.
Disposition is decided by the defined process, not unilaterally.

options.text: Adjust the drawing to match the part
Ignore it if it is close
options.rationale: Out-of-tolerance parts must be handled, not ignored.

items.explanation: Correct: nonconforming material is recorded and quarantined for a disposition decision.

items.stem: Reporting a measurement of 12.3456 mm from a gauge that resolves to 0.01 mm is wrong because it:

options.text: Claims more precision than the instrument can provide
options.rationale: Correct: reported digits must match the instrument resolution.
The issue is false precision, not magnitude.
The unit is correct; the precision is not.
Calibration is separate from reporting resolution.

items.explanation: Correct: reported digits must match the instrument resolution.

items.stem: Select TWO reasons acceptance sampling is used instead of 100% inspection.

options.text: It is faster and lower cost for large lots
options.rationale: Correct: sampling reduces time and cost on large lots.
Correct: destructive tests cannot be applied to every unit.

options.text: It guarantees zero defective units ship
options.rationale: Sampling accepts some risk; it does not guarantee zero defects.

options.text: It removes the need for drawings

items.explanation: Correct: sampling reduces time and cost on large lots. Correct: destructive tests cannot be applied to every unit.
